limits: No experiments; statistics and incidents are asserted without citations (Gartner 40% by 2027, 73%/$4.8M vs 97%/$4.4M).
LLM Guard code listing is truncated in the PDF and the chapter reports no results for it.
Mitigations are generic; no evidence of effectiveness against prompt injection is given beyond PINT scores for two products.
Conclusion mentions fine-tuning as covered but the chapter has no fine-tuning section.
Fast-moving tools and benchmarks (PINT, BIPIA, Garak, PyRIT, DeepTeam) date quickly.
practices: Give each agent scoped roles and permissions via RBAC, reviewed periodically (Safeguards).
Enforce behavior constraints through a policy enforcement layer that validates every decision or action against rules (Safeguards, Internal Failures).
Isolate agent operations with sandboxing or containers to limit blast radius (Safeguards).
Validate inputs and outputs with pipelines on both sides of the agent (Safeguards).
Apply rate limiting and anomaly detection; log every decision immutably and encrypted (Safeguards).
Provide fallback and fail-safe states that revert to safe workflow or escalate to a human (Safeguards).
Use input sanitisation, instruction anchoring and prompt templates against prompt injection; test with PINT and BIPIA (Defensive Techniques).
Red team continuously with automated tools (DeepTeam, Garak, PyRIT) plus human testers; feed findings into filters and config (Red Teaming).
Threat model with MAESTRO: diagram system, assess assets and entry points per layer, score risks, simulate attacks (MAESTRO).
Minimise data, encrypt at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS, mTLS), purge logs and caches by retention policy (Data Privacy).
Hash (SHA-256) and sign incoming data, revalidate at each stage, use append-only logs (Data Provenance).
Use RBAC/ABAC with read-only or write-only granularity for sensitive data; sanitise logs (Handling Sensitive Data).
Segment networks (DMZ, subnets, ACLs), mTLS, OAuth 2.0 or API keys, SCA and SBOM for supply chain, honeytokens (External Threats).
Monitor KPIs: error rate >5%/hr, P99 latency >2 s, 80% sustained utilisation, similarity <0.85, any state race (Internal Failures).
Use idempotent and transactional operations, dependency isolation, quorum voting for multiagent consensus (Internal Failures).
Run chaos engineering: fault injection, game days, blast radius control, postmortems (Internal Failures).
Mitigate human-in-the-loop weaknesses with escalation paths, adaptive alerting and operator training (Unique Risks).

terms.definition: Agents may interpret their objectives differently than intended, especially when tasked with vague or ambiguous instructions.
Humans may over-trust agent recommendations, failing to adequately scrutinize outputs.
Continuous or low-priority alerts lead operators to overlook critical warnings.
The model's primary instructions are strongly reinforced throughout the prompt.
A proactive security practice where experts simulate adversarial attacks to identify vulnerabilities, weaknesses, and failure modes.
Multi-Agent Environment, Security, Threat, Risk, and Outcome: a CSA threat modeling framework with seven layers.
The ability to track the lineage and history of data, including where it originated, how it has been processed, and which transformations it has undergone.
Fake pieces of sensitive information embedded in data flows to detect unauthorized access.
Isolating agent operations from the broader system via sandboxing or containerization.
